title: Task Operators and Geometric Samplers

blocks.md: This lesson covers the book's section on **Task Operators and Geometric Samplers**. Read the excerpt, then test yourself below.

blocks.source: Vol IV, Grounded Intent, § Task Operators and Geometric Samplers
blocks.md: A symbolic task planner can emit the discrete action `Grasp(Mug, Handle)` and mark the mug as held in its internal state even when no collision-free inverse kinematics solution reaches the handle, a bin wall blocks the approach, or the mug has not been separated from adjacent items on the belt. The high-level action `Grasp(Mug, Handle)` inherits from classical planning traditions, where actions are formalized as **operators** defined by preconditions, an add list, and a delete list.

blocks.prompt: Think first: In two or three sentences, explain why Task and motion planning matters for the system this section describes.
blocks.md: Compare your answer with the book's claim: Task and motion planning certifies symbolic facts with geometric samplers, whether a classical planner or a language model wrote the plan.

questions.q: The section **Task Operators and Geometric Samplers** develops one of the chapter's claims. Which one?
options: A conformal predictor returns a set of candidate answers whose threshold is calibrated on held-out labeled cases, keeping every candidate it cannot exclude and giving a chosen coverage rate under exchangeability.
A grasp has force closure when its contacts can resist any external wrench within the friction cones, which bounds stability, not the magnitude of the squeeze.

The admissible goal set is fixed by the verified task profile from what the grasp can physically absorb, not estimated by the proposer, and the proposal's error envelope plus tracking reserve must fit inside it.
Task and motion planning certifies symbolic facts with geometric samplers, whether a classical planner or a language model wrote the plan.
